newsitem.title: FRANCE: US Ex-Secretary Cheney holds oil talks in Algiers.
newsitem.headline: US Ex-Secretary Cheney holds oil talks in Algiers.

text.p: U.S. former Defence Secretary Dick Cheney, current chairman of U.S.-based Halliburton Co, on Wednesday held talks with senior Algerian officials on oil and gas cooperation, said the official Algerian news agency APS.

Cheney, who arrived on Tuesday at the Southern Hassi Messaoud province where Algeria's main oil field is located, met separately Energy and Mining Minister Amar Makhloufi and secretary of state in charge of cooperation and Maghreb affairs Lahcene Moussaoui in Algiers.

"Talks between Cheney and Makhloufi focused on cooperation and partnership between the (Algerian oil and gas state-owned) Sonatrach and Halliburton group," said APS adding that Cheny also discussed energy partnership with Moussaoui.

Halliburton and Anadarko Petroleum Corp signed in September last year a $177 million agreement with Sonatrach to develop the southern field of Hassi Berkine in the southern basin of Ghadmes, in the Sahara, where 34 of Algeria's 207 discoveries lie.
Oil and gas dominate Algeria's economy with the country's exports value of oil and gas amounting $12.6 billion in 1996, up 29 percent from 1995.
